title: Count Everything
topic: Count squares, groups, handshakes, outfits and pairs with a system

items.q: A grid has 3 rows with 4 squares in each row. How many squares are in the grid?
items.hint: Count the squares in one row. Then add the rows.

slips.say: 7 is 3 and 4 added. Add 4 three times.

tpl.q: A grid has {r} rows with {c} squares in each row. How many squares are in the grid?
tpl.hint: Count the squares in one row. Then add the rows.
steps: Add {c} once for each row: {ans} squares.

items.q: 4 bags have 3 sweets in each bag. How many sweets are there in all?
items.hint: Add the sweets in each bag.

slips.say: Do not add 4 and 3 only. Add 3 once for each bag.

tpl.q: {a} bags have {b} sweets in each bag. How many sweets are there in all?
tpl.hint: Add the sweets in each bag.
steps: Add {b} once for each bag: {ans} sweets.

items.q: Three friends shake hands once with each other. How many handshakes are there?
items.hint: List the pairs: A with B, A with C, then B with C.
steps: B with C. That is 3 handshakes.

slips.say: B with A is the same handshake as A with B. Count each pair once.

items.q: A child lists handshakes: A with B, A with C, B with A, B with C. Which one is a repeat?
items.hint: Which pair has the same two letters as an earlier pair?
steps: A with B and B with A have the same two letters.
B with A is the repeat.

slips.say: A with B comes first. Which pair comes again with the letters the other way round?

items.q: Ali has 2 hats and 3 scarves. Each hat goes with each scarf. How many ways can he wear one hat and one scarf?
items.hint: Each hat goes with every scarf.

slips.say: Do not add 2 and 3. Each hat goes with every scarf.

tpl.q: Ali has {h} hats and {s} scarves. Each hat goes with each scarf. How many ways can he wear one hat and one scarf?
tpl.hint: Each hat goes with every scarf.
steps: Add {s} once for each hat: {ans} ways.

items.q: 5 children shake hands once with every other child. How many handshakes are there?
items.hint: Count only the new handshakes: 4, then 3, then 2, then 1.
steps: The next makes 3 new ones, then 2, then 1.

slips.say: That counts every handshake twice. Count only the new ones.

tpl.q: {n} children shake hands once with every other child. How many handshakes are there?
tpl.hint: Count only the new handshakes each time.
steps: The first child makes the most handshakes.
Each next child makes one fewer new handshake.

items.q: How many squares of any size are in a 2 by 2 grid?
items.hint: Count the small squares first. Then look for a bigger one.
steps: The whole grid is 1 big square.

slips.say: The whole grid is a square too. Count the big one.

tpl.q: How many squares of any size are in a {k} by {k} grid?
tpl.hint: Count the small squares first. Then look for bigger ones.
steps: Then count the bigger squares of each size.

items.q: How many pairs of whole numbers make 8? Count 1 + 7, then 2 + 6, and so on. The same two numbers in another order are the same pair.
items.hint: Start at 1. Stop when the pairs repeat.

tpl.q: How many pairs of whole numbers make {t}? Start at 1. The same two numbers in another order are the same pair.
tpl.hint: Start at 1. Stop when the pairs repeat.

items.q: There are 2 paths from Home to the Park and 4 paths from the Park to School. There is also 1 direct path from Home to School. How many ways are there from Home to School?
items.hint: Each path to the Park goes with each path from the Park.
steps: Each of the 2 first paths goes with each of the 4 second paths: 8 ways.

slips.say: 2 and 4 are not added. Each first path goes with every second path.

tpl.q: There are {a} paths from Home to the Park and {b} paths from the Park to School. There is also 1 direct path from Home to School. How many ways are there from Home to School?
tpl.hint: Each path to the Park goes with each path from the Park.
steps: Each of the {a} first paths goes with each of the {b} second paths.

items.q: How many squares of any size are in a 4 by 4 grid?
items.hint: Count by size: 1 by 1, then 2 by 2, then 3 by 3, then 4 by 4.

slips.say: There are bigger squares too: 2 by 2, 3 by 3 and 4 by 4.

items.q: Make a counting puzzle for a grown-up with pairs, outfits or handshakes. Check your answer with a list or a table.
items.hint: Use a list with a rule.
steps: Write the puzzle and the answer.
Ask a grown-up to check it with a list.

items.q: A ruler costs $6 and a glue stick costs $5. How much do they cost altogether?

slips.say: 1 is the gap. Altogether means add the two prices.

tpl.q: A ruler costs {a|usd} and a glue stick costs {b|usd}. How much do they cost altogether?
